correctness.rationale: The ordered-subsequence capacity criterion is an iff: m+1 overlapping intervals forbid a schedule, while cyclic coloring attains one if spaced endpoints are disjoint. Dominance induction over earliest accepted indices proves greedy cardinality optimal at each prefix. Cyclic counts certify EFX. The m-1 long + 3 short example forces loads (3,1,...,1); removing one long yields (2,1,...,1), while every feasible family of <=m+1 jobs can be fairly assigned by extracting an existing compatible pair. Half-open ties and nondecreasing endpoints checked. Exact rational CHECK.py passed 14,965 tests; it does not stand in for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The closest fair scheduling paper addresses arbitrary interval streams and bounds their price, not the exact optimal prefix-EFX/structural threshold stated here. Proper interval online coloring literature assumes different arrival and minimizes colors rather than maximizing accepted jobs with fair loads. Classical equitable coloring of claw-free graphs covers part of offline existence, so that part is explicitly credited and not marketed as independent novelty. Queries to a semantic research index, primary studies and prior claims revealed no matching combined statement. Unindexed implication risk remains; no uniqueness is inferred from database partition.
residual_risks: The static proper-interval equitable coloring component is known; the combined theorem may be an unstated easy corollary in older interval-scheduling theory.
The full text of online proper-interval coloring and the original de Werra proof was not exhaustively inspected, and terminology for fair machine loading varies.
Semantic index non-matches and role partitions are not novelty certificates.

The new minimal nested witness is conceptually close to the published unweighted long-versus-short lower-bound construction; only the thin-nesting and universal minimality refinements are asserted beyond that motif.

value.rationale: The motivating paper provides an exact worst-case online fair penalty in general streams. A no-nesting geometric restriction is natural in scheduling, and the proposed policy achieves an optimal ratio simultaneously after every input prefix without revocation. The m+2 minimality and arbitrarily small nesting family identify an exact structural boundary rather than a routine finite instance. This clarifies which interval geometry, not just task length variability, creates a fairness-efficiency tradeoff.
